response.text:
Short answer up front: archiving removes messages from your Inbox but keeps them (and any labels) in your account; deleting moves messages to Trash (recoverable for ~30 days) and then permanently removes them — and deleting a label is different from deleting the messages that have that label.

Details and practical differences

- Archive (messages):
  - What happens: removes the Inbox label/visibility. Messages remain in All Mail and keep any user labels (e.g., "Contracts 2019").
  - Visibility: you can still find them via the Contracts 2019 label, All Mail, or search.
  - Recovery / permanence: archived messages are not deleted — reversible at any time.
  - Storage: does not free storage space.

- Delete (messages):
  - What happens: messages are moved to Trash. They are removed from label views and Inbox in the normal listing.
  - Recovery / permanence: items in Trash can be restored within ~30 days (or until you empty Trash). After that they’re permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  - Storage: permanently deleting messages frees storage (only after Trash is emptied or retention expires).

- Delete a label (not the messages):
  - What happens: the label name is removed from messages, but the messages themselves remain in your account (All Mail / search). Deleting a label does not move messages to Trash.
  - Storage: deleting the label does not free storage because messages still exist.

Other notes
- If a message has multiple labels, deleting one label does not delete the message as long as it exists elsewhere (All Mail).
- Threads/conversations: actions apply to the whole conversation view in Gmail.
- If you’re worried about accidentally losing attachments or important content, deleting is the risky one because of permanent removal after Trash is emptied.

Recommendation
- If you’re unsure, archive — it’s safe and reversible.
- If you might want to delete but want a backup first, export or download the messages (or use Google Takeout) before deleting.
- If you meant “delete the label” and just want the label gone while keeping the messages, that’s safe: messages remain.

If you want, tell me exactly which action you’re considering (delete messages, delete label, or archive all messages under that label) and I’ll give precise step-by-step instructions and a safe checklist.
